candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44(d) require limits in addition to, or more stringent than effluent limitation guidelines (technology based). NM WQS that are more stringent than effluent limitation guideline and applicable for this discharge are based on 20.6.4 NMAC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether WQS-based limits under 20.6.4 NMAC supersede or supplement technology-based limits determines which numeric limits are enforceable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Stream segment specific (20.6.4.401 NMAC) WQS for pH, 6.6 to 9.0 standard units (s.u.), are more restrictive than the technology-based limits presented earlier and downstream Navajo Nation segment specific WQS for pH (i.e., 5-9 s.u. for domestic water supply, 6.5-9 s.u. for agricultural water supply, etc.). The pH limits of 6.6 to 9.0 s.u. in the previous permit, which are protective of the downstream Navajo Nation standards, will be continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which pH numeric range (6.6–9.0 s.u. vs. other cited downstream standards) applies, and whether limits carried from the previous permit into the draft permit are operative, changes the enforceable pH limit used to evaluate reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Primary contact currently is one of the designated uses of State of New Mexico Segment No. 20.6.4.401 of the San Juan basin. The State of New Mexico WQS criteria applicable to the primary contact designated use of the receiving stream are the monthly geometric mean of E. coli bacteria of 126 cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL) and single sample of 410 cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether primary contact is the governing designated use selects the 126/410 cfu/100 mL criteria as applicable limits (A) and frames which bacteria monitoring expectations attach to the discharge (B).

candidates.exact_span: The results for E. coli may be reported as either colony forming units (CFU) or the most probable number (MPN) depending on the analytical method used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether CFU and MPN results are treated as equivalent numeric results for limit comparison (A) or as differently qualified evidence affects classification of reported vs. missing/no-data monitoring outcomes (C).

candidates.exact_span:
Daily mass loading limit, cfu/day = C, cfu/100 mL * 1,000 mL/L * l/0.264 gallons * Q, flow, expressed in 1,000,000 gallons/day

Where:
C = state water quality standard criterion for bacteria, 126 cfu/100 mL
Q = stream flow in million gallons per day (mgd), 299 MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of the stated formula inputs (C=126, Q=299 MGD) or conversion factors change the derived daily mass loading limit magnitude used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli daily mass loading limit of 3.19 x 1010 cfu/day in the TMDL was established
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the TMDL daily mass loading limit is an enforceable numeric discharge limit versus background rationale changes which limit value applies to mass-loading measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Downstream Navajo Nation segment specific WQS for E. coli bacteria are 126 cfu/100 mL monthly geometric mean for domestic water supply, and 235 cfu/100 mL to 575 cfu/100 mL single sample maximum for secondary human contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which downstream Navajo Nation criterion (domestic geometric mean vs. secondary-contact single-sample range) governs when multiple limits are cited changes the applicable numeric bacteria limits.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monthly geometric mean limit of 126 cfu/100 mL, daily maximum limit of 235 cfu/100 mL and daily maximum mass loading limit of 3.19 x 1010 cfu/day in the previous permit will be continued in the draft permit to be consistent with the New Mexico TMDL and protective of the more stringent NNWQS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage bundles three distinct limit types (geometric mean, daily maximum concentration, daily mass loading); different readings of which are continued and operative change which limit applies to a given reported parameter and monitoring period.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monitoring frequency requirement in the previous permit be also continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether monitoring frequency obligations from the previous permit carry forward into the draft permit determines if monitoring was required for evaluated periods (B) and how to classify intervals with no reported result against an expected monitoring schedule (C).
